# Repair defects and untested criteria as units of work of their own
## Intent

A defect the loop files today stays filed. Each package's scope rules stop
it from touching an earlier package's code, so a later package that meets a
defect works around it and leaves it in place, and the backlog only grows.
A repair is a unit of work of its own: one session, one issue, one branch,
one merge. It proves the defect with a test before it fixes anything, and
the same run shows when a later package already fixed it. `specrun` runs
repairs at two moments: instead of stopping, after a package opened a
serious defect, and in batches after every reconcile, most severe first, so
that correctness and minor defects and untested criteria get closed without
halting the loop. It chooses what to repair from labels and checks from the
forge and the repository what each session left.

## Goals

- **A repair queue from labels.** After each reconcile `specrun` queues the
  open defects whose severity is in `--repair-on` and the open untested
  items, most severe first, then oldest first, at most `--repair-max` per
  reconcile, leaving out issues labelled `af:repair-failed` and, unless
  `--repair-security` is set, security defects.
- **Repair instead of stopping.** With `--repair`, a package that opened
  defects of a severity in `--stop-on` gets each of them repaired before the
  next package.
- **A repair proves the defect first.** The regression test is written and
  run on the unchanged code; a test that passes there is committed alone and
  closes the issue as already fixed.
- **An untested criterion is closed by a test**, or becomes a defect and is
  repaired as one in the same session.
- **A failed repair is marked and left.** It gets `af:repair-failed` and a
  comment; later queues leave it out until a person removes the label.
- **Every repair session is checked**: back on a clean base branch, the
  issue closed or labelled `af:repair-failed`.

## Non-goals

- **Repairing security defects without a person.** A repair session may fix
  one, but only with `--repair-security`; the default is to stop.
- **A recipe for a slow test suite.** A `test-cost` finding is a minor
  defect and is repaired like one; how a suite is made cheaper is decided
  in that repair or by a person.
- **Moving task state.** A repair is not a package task and writes no
  `progress.json`.

## Background

`22_open_items_read_back` stops the loop after a package opened a defect of
a severity in `--stop-on`. `23_specrun_reconcile` runs a reconcile every few
packages, turns a rejected deviation into a `correctness` defect and leaves
the labels as they should stand. Nothing fixes a defect: on the measured
repository 13 were open after 25 packages, and none of the later packages
addressed one. af-impl has a package mode and a reconcile mode and no way to
work on a single issue. `specrun` has two kinds of step, a package and a
reconcile, each with a ledger line and a check of what the session left.

## Requirements

### 1. The repair queue

At each reconcile, after its rules, `specrun` builds the queue from the
labels as they stand: every open `af:defect` whose severity is in
`--repair-on` (default `security,data-loss,correctness,minor,untested`), and
every open `af:untested` item when `--repair-on` holds `untested`. It leaves
out every issue labelled `af:repair-failed`, and every `security` defect
unless `--repair-security` is set. It orders the queue most severe first
(`security`, `data-loss`, `correctness`, `minor`, then `untested`), then
oldest first, and takes at most `--repair-max` (default 5). It repairs them
one session each, in order, before the next package. Issues not taken stay
for the next reconcile. The queue is in the state file.

### 2. A repair step

`specrun` starts `claude -p "/af-impl --repair <issue number>"` with the
flags of every session; the stall rule applies. When the session ends it
checks that the base branch is checked out and the tree is clean, and that
the issue is closed or labelled `af:repair-failed`. A session that leaves
anything else stops the loop.

The outcome goes into the ledger: `fixed`, `already_fixed` or `failed`. A
failed repair whose issue has a severity in `--stop-on` stops the loop;
otherwise the loop goes on. A repair step recorded as running when
`specrun` starts counts as done when its issue is closed, and is run again
otherwise.

### 3. Repair instead of stopping

With `--repair`, after a package that opened defects whose severity is in
`--stop-on`, `specrun` repairs each of them, most severe first, before the
next package, instead of stopping. A `security` defect is repaired only
when `--repair-security` is also set; without it `specrun` stops as before.
After the repairs it makes the stop check again: a defect that is still
open stops the loop.

### 4. What a repair session does (af-impl text)

A repair of a **defect**:

- branches `fix/<issue>-<slug>` from the base branch;
- writes the regression test first and runs it on the unchanged code;
- when the test fails, fixes the code until the test passes;
- when the test passes on the unchanged code, fixes nothing: the defect is
  already gone. It commits only the test, with a `test:` commit that says
  so, and closes the issue with that test as evidence;
- passes the full gate (`speca --gate full`) and, when the issue's package
  has `test_commands`, that package's commands;
- merges `--no-ff` and closes the issue with the merge commit as evidence.

A repair of an **untested** item writes the test the criterion is missing,
on a `fix/<issue>-<slug>` branch, and runs it on the unchanged code. When it
passes, the repair commits the test (`test:`), passes the full gate, merges
and closes the issue with the test as evidence. When it fails, the repair
relabels the issue `af:defect` with severity `correctness`, with a comment
holding the failure, and goes on as a repair of that defect, in the same
session.

A repair touches only what the fix needs, and may edit a landed package's
code, because the defect is its scope. It fails when its test cannot
reproduce the issue as described, in which case it does not guess, or when
it cannot fix the defect in two attempts. Either way it comments on the
issue with what it tried, adds `af:repair-failed`, leaves the issue open and
returns to a clean base branch. The merge commit of a repair ends with an
`AF-Run:` trailer whose `repair` object holds the issue and the outcome.

### 5. Configuration and the dry run

`--repair`, `--repair-on`, `--repair-max` and `--repair-security` are flags,
each with its `SPECRUN_` variable. `specrun --dry-run` prints the repair
queue as the labels now stand.

## Design Decisions

1. **Repairs are separate merges, and `security` stops by default** (PRD
   decision 9). A repair edits code another package landed; inside a
   package's branch it would break that package's scope and traceability.
2. **A repair proves the defect before it fixes it** (PRD decision 14).
3. **Stopping and repairing are configured separately** (PRD decision 17).
   Batching repairs at reconciles, with a cap, keeps their time bounded and
   visible in the ledger.
4. **An untested criterion is closed by a test** (PRD decision 18).
5. **`specrun` reads the outcome from the forge and the trailer.** Closed
   means repaired, `af:repair-failed` means failed, and the trailer's
   `repair.outcome` tells `already_fixed` from `fixed`; a closed issue with
   no trailer is `fixed`.
6. **`untested` is a value of `--repair-on`.** The PRD's default list and
   its "when `--repair-on` holds `untested`" make it one; it sorts after
   every severity.
7. **A failed repair of a serious defect stops the loop, and so does a
   serious defect the repairs left open.** `--repair` replaces a stop only
   when the repair succeeds.
8. **`--repair-max 0` repairs nothing at a reconcile.** The repairs that
   `--repair` runs instead of stopping are not capped: each of them stands
   between the loop and the next package.
9. **The queue is rebuilt at every reconcile.** What the state file holds is
   only the rest of the current batch, so labels a person changed in between
   are honoured.

## Dependencies

- `23_specrun_reconcile` (active): the reconcile after which the queue is
  built, and the rejected deviations that become defects.
- `22_open_items_read_back` (active): `--stop-on` and the stop rule that
  `--repair` replaces.
- `19_speca_gate` (active): `speca --gate full`, which a repair runs.
- `aflib/issuex`; the `issue` command, which the session uses.
- The af-impl skill (`skills/af-impl`), which gains the `--repair` mode.

## Glossary

- **repair**: one session that closes one defect or one untested item on a
  branch and a merge of its own.
- **repair queue**: the issues `specrun` will repair after a reconcile, in
  order.
- **already fixed**: a defect whose regression test passes on the unchanged
  code.

   → the queue is ordered `security`, `data-loss`, `correctness`, `minor`, then `untested`, and within one of them oldest first by creation time; it holds at most `--repair-max` issues, 5 when the flag is absent; the issues beyond the cap are not repaired before the next reconcile

### REQ-3: Repair a serious defect instead of stopping

**Rationale:** Stopping is right when nobody is there to decide; with permission to repair, the loop can clear the defect and go on.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHERE `--repair` is given and a package has landed with open defects of a severity in `--stop-on`, THE specrun SHALL repair each of them, most severe first then oldest first, before the next package, and make the stop check again afterwards
   → the sessions after the package are one repair per such defect, with no cap; when every one is closed the next package starts; a defect that is still open after its repair stops the loop as the stop rule does
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
   ```
   in internal/specrun/repair_test.go, a table with --repair and --repair-security over what the fake session of 01 leaves and what the repairs do: {data-loss and security, both fixed -> prompts [01, repair security, repair data-loss, 02]; data-loss, repair marks it failed -> exit code 1 after one repair; a correctness defect alone -> no repair, 02 starts}
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF `--repair` is given without `--repair-security` and a package has landed with an open `security` defect, THEN THE specrun SHALL stop the loop without repairing it
   → exit code 1 with the stop rule's `result.stopped`; no repair session starts for the security defect
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
   ```
   in internal/specrun/repair_test.go: with --repair and a fake session of 01 that leaves a security defect and a data-loss defect: assert exit code 1, result.stopped.issues names the security defect, and no session started after 01
   ```

### REQ-4: Show the repair queue in a dry run

**Rationale:** A person deciding whether to allow repairs wants to see what would be repaired.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHERE `--dry-run` is given and a forge client can be made, THE specrun SHALL report the repair queue as the labels now stand
   → `result.repair_queue` lists each issue with its number, title, URL and severity or `untested`, in queue order and capped by `--repair-max`; it is `[]` when the queue is empty; no session starts and the forge records no write
   Check: integration
   - setup: the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
   ```
   in internal/specrun/repair_test.go: with open defects minor and correctness and an untested item: run --dry-run --repair-max 2; assert result.repair_queue names the correctness and the minor defect in that order; assert no session and no forge write
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: specrun repairs a defect and an untested item after a reconcile

1. **operator** runs `specrun --reconcile-every 1` with an open correctness defect and an open untested item on the forge
2. **specrun** lands the next package, runs the reconcile and builds the repair queue from the labels: the defect, then the untested item
3. **specrun** starts a repair session for the defect
4. **session** branches, writes the regression test, sees it fail, fixes the code, passes the full gate that speca runs, merges and closes the issue
5. **speca** runs the full gate for the repair and answers `pass`
6. **specrun** checks the base branch and the issue, records `fixed`, and starts the repair of the untested item
7. **session** writes the missing test, sees it pass on the unchanged code, commits it, merges and closes the issue with an `already_fixed` trailer
8. **specrun** records `already_fixed` and goes on to the next package

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** specrun's Main, afspec, git, the fake claude as a real process, the queue and the repair checks against the in-memory issuex client, the ledger on disk

**Setup:**

- the fixture repository, the fake claude and the in-memory issuex client of internal/specrun's helpers
- two open packages; on the forge an open issue with af:defect, af:severity-correctness, af:from-00 and an older open issue with af:untested, af:from-00; fake repair sessions that merge a fix branch into main, close their issue and end the merge commit with an AF-Run trailer naming the issue and the outcome

**End state:**

- the session prompts are the package, the reconcile, the repair of the defect, the repair of the untested item, then the second package
- both issues are closed
- the ledger holds a repair line with outcome fixed and one with already_fixed
- main holds both merge commits and the tree is clean

**Pseudocode:**

```
in cmd/specrun/main_test.go, beside the existing end-to-end tests: code = Main(['--reconcile-every', '1', '--max', '2']); assert prompts[:5] == ['/af-impl .specs/01_…', '/af-impl --reconcile …', '/af-impl --repair <defect>', '/af-impl --repair <untested>', '/af-impl .specs/02_…']; assert both issues closed; assert outcomes of the repair lines == ['fixed', 'already_fixed']; assert git status is clean on main
```

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-2.1

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the queue table, the session order after a reconcile, the restart with a rest of a queue and the flag tables as tests and confirm they fail; teach the fake claude a repair script: merge a fix branch with or without a trailer, close the issue, add af:repair-failed, or misbehave
- 1.2 Add the flags --repair, --repair-on, --repair-max and --repair-security with their SPECRUN_ variables: --repair-on a comma-separated list of the four severities and untested, default all five, the empty string none; --repair-max an integer, default 5, 0 none; refuse other values as usage errors
- 1.3 Add the function that builds the queue from the open issues and the flags: defects whose one severity is in --repair-on, untested items when it holds untested, without af:repair-failed, without security unless --repair-security; ordered security, data-loss, correctness, minor, untested, then by creation time; cut to --repair-max
- 1.4 After the rules of a reconcile build the queue, write it to the state file, and make the next steps one repair per issue in order, removing each from the stored queue as its step ends; at the next reconcile the queue is built anew
- 1.5 Start a repair step's session with the prompt `/af-impl --repair <issue number>` and everything else as for a package; name the step <n>-repair-<issue number>

### 4. Give af-impl its repair mode (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2.1

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Extend the fake session's repair script and the end-to-end test so that the prompt and the trailer are the ones the skill documents
- 4.2 Add skills/af-impl/references/repair.md and link it from SKILL.md: `/af-impl --repair <issue>` implements no package and moves no task state; it reads the issue with `issue <ref>`, refuses one that is closed or carries neither af:defect nor af:untested, and may edit a landed package's code, because the defect is its scope
- 4.3 A defect, in that file: branch fix/<issue>-<slug> from the up-to-date base branch; write the regression test first and run it on the unchanged code, keeping the command and its output; when it fails, fix the code until it passes, touching only what the fix needs; when it passes on the unchanged code, fix nothing, commit only the test as `test: <subject>` saying the defect was already gone, and close the issue with that test as evidence
- 4.4 Then, in that file: pass `speca <package> --gate full` for the issue's package and, when that package has test_commands, those commands; merge --no-ff into the base branch on a passing gate on the merged tree; push; close the issue with `issue <ref> --close --body` naming the merge commit and the test; end the merge commit message with `AF-Run: {"repair":{"issue":<number>,"outcome":"fixed"}}`, or already_fixed
- 4.5 An untested item, in that file: write the test the criterion is missing on a fix/<issue>-<slug> branch and run it on the unchanged code; when it passes, commit it as `test:`, pass the full gate, merge and close the issue with the test as evidence, outcome already_fixed; when it fails, relabel the issue af:defect with af:severity-correctness and a comment holding the failure, and go on as a repair of that defect in the same session
- 4.6 Failing, in that file: when the test cannot reproduce the issue as it is described, for example because it names code that no longer exists, do not guess; when the defect is not fixed after two attempts, stop. Either way comment on the issue with what was tried, add af:repair-failed, leave the issue open, discard the branch's uncommitted work and return to a clean base branch
- 4.7 In SKILL.md name the mode in the argument hint and in §1, and extend the last rule of *Never* to the issue a repair was given; keep the rendered body under the ceiling `make skills-check` enforces

**Touches:**

- `skills/af-impl/SKILL.md`
- `skills/af-impl/references/repair.md`
- `internal/specrun/`
- `cmd/specrun/main_test.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `make test` passes
- `make lint` passes
- `make skills-check` passes

**Depends on:** 1, 2, 3, 4

- 5.2 Trace PATH-1 through the real code; confirm each step calls the next and no stub remains
